transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2028-08-30 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 min
- Location: Zoom
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Derek Alvarez (Redwood SE), Kelsey Park (Redwood SE), Priya Nambiar (BlueHarbor), Jonas Keller (BlueHarbor), Fatima Ruiz (BlueHarbor Proc), Ethan Lowe (BlueHarbor Sec)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Intro + channel/partner goals (BlueHarbor wants hybrid onramp for enterprise SaaS customers)
- Technical constraints: VPC peering, private deployment options, NVLink/multi-GPU for high throughput, KMS integration, SOC2 and audit logs
- Agreed pilot: 4-week focused POC to validate throughput/latency on BlueHarbor workloads; Redwood to run micro-benchmarks and share findings

Topics covered: partner GTM alignment, integration points (APIs, agent/sidecar), security/compliance, pilot scoping, pricing model options, ops handoff

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call — I'll kick off, I'm Maya, AE, Derek is our solution engineer, Kelsey joins for integration details.
[00:18] Priya (BlueHarbor): Hi Maya, hey Derek, thanks. I'm Priya head of platform at BlueHarbor, with Jonas our cloud arch and Ethan for security. Fatima from procurement will drop in questions later.
[00:34] Derek (Redwood): Cool, thanks. agenda for today is to understand your channel goals, high-level infra constraints, and see where Redwood fits — hosted vs dedicated vs private. Sorry if my mic is fuzzy.
[00:47] Jonas (BlueHarbor): We run a multi-tenant SaaS with bursty inference for customer-facing features, and we already resell GPU credits via our marketplace so partner fit is important. We're exploring both integrated hosted flows and on-prem agents for bigger customers.
[01:05] Maya (Redwood): Understood. quick clarifying q: are your customers asking for fully private VPC peering or will customer-managed VMs be enough?
[01:18] Priya (BlueHarbor): 70% want VPC peering or private link. A few will accept multi-tenant hosted if we can guarantee no chatter and clear data retention.
[01:32] Ethan (BlueHarbor): From security standpoint — we need KMS/HSM support, audit logs per tenant, and SOC2 plus EU data residency for some accounts.
[01:45] Kelsey (Redwood): That's in scope. Redwood Private supports VPC + on-prem packaging, and we offer KMS integrations. small caveat — on-prem adds ops work, and kernel/quantization choices change perf.
[02:02] Jonas (BlueHarbor): When you say quantization choices — do you mean we have to pick q8 vs q4 and that affects latency/quality? we saw weird hallucinations with some quantized variants earlier.
[02:17] Derek (Redwood): Yeah, exactly. quantization profile affects numeric fidelity. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles based on evals; for chat-style workloads we tend to avoid aggressive q4 if it hurts safety. We'll run evals on your prompt set in the pilot.
[02:35] Priya (BlueHarbor): For the pilot we want to validate 99p latency < 200ms for small replies and throughput ~500 qps for batch scoring. Is that realistic?
[02:48] Derek (Redwood): 200ms 99p for short generations is tight but possible on dedicated NVLink multi-GPU with optimized kernels and prefix caching. For 500 qps we need batching and KV cache configured; depends on model context length.
[03:05] Jonas (BlueHarbor): Our typical context is 512 tokens, average generation 30 tokens. models: mostly open Llama-3 style variants and some proprietary fine-tuned customer models.
[03:19] Maya (Redwood): Good detail. We should benchmark Llama-3 quantized and a tuned variant. also need to know if you require model residency — i.e., customer cannot share models off your cluster.
[03:33] Priya (BlueHarbor): For top-tier customers, yes model residency + dedicated capacity is needed. for others, shared hosted is ok.
[03:41] Ethan (BlueHarbor): Also we need encryption-at-rest in our KMS and customer-controlled keys. Can Redwood use our cloud KMS?
[03:50] Kelsey (Redwood): Yes, we support customer-managed KMS in Redwood Private; HSM integrations on request. we will share the KMS integration guide.
[04:02] Maya (Redwood): quick note, we have a SOC2 lite summary and an architecture diagram. I'll share after the call.
[04:10] Fatima (BlueHarbor): (entering) hi all, quick procurement q — what's the usual commitment for Dedicated? monthly reserved?
[04:20] Maya (Redwood): usually reserved monthly/annual commits for Dedicated; pilot can be consumption with a short reserved window if you want to test. we'll send pricing scenarios.
[04:34] Jonas (BlueHarbor): On the infra side we need to know GPU families you support for on-prem — A100, H100, 80GB, and do you have recommended NVLink topology?
[04:47] Derek (Redwood): We run on H100s primarily in Dedicated; H100 80GB with NVLink interconnect for multi-gpu is our baseline for high-throughput. for on-prem we can adapt to A100s but perf differs. We'll provide a recommended rack layout and nvlink lanes guidance.
[05:08] Priya (BlueHarbor): How about multi-tenancy — can we pin a physical pool for certain customers?
[05:18] Kelsey (Redwood): Yes, Dedicated pools can be reserved per-tenant or per-customer group. We also do automatic fallback to hosted variants if capacity is exhausted, configurable by policy.
[05:30] Jonas (BlueHarbor): latency vs cost trade-offs — curious if Redwood Optimize can give actionable delta numbers?
[05:38] Derek (Redwood): Absolutely, Optimize will recommend batching window, quantization, and cache TTLs with estimated token cost impact. We'll run it against your sample workloads.
[05:50] Priya (BlueHarbor): On connectivity: VPC peering, private link, or an edge agent? we prefer peering for largest customers but suburban/leasing carriers prefer agent.
[06:03] Maya (Redwood): We support all three patterns. edge agent is lighter for networks that block peering but requires a sidecar and some NAT rules. peering gives the cleanest security posture.
[06:13] Ethan (BlueHarbor): audit logs — per-tenant, read-only exports every 30 days is fine. can we get immutable logs for compliance?
[06:22] Kelsey (Redwood): We can retain logs per retention policy. immutable export to your S3 or GCS bucket is supported. we'll include retention SLA options.
[06:33] Jonas (BlueHarbor): about the Pilot — want to align scope: 4 weeks, three customer personas, models (Llama-3-tuned, Llama-3-base), metrics (99p latency, p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens), and failover behavior.
[06:50] Derek (Redwood): Sounds good. Derek: for the bench we need sample prompts + the top 10 endpoint patterns. Priya can you share that artifact?
[07:02] Priya (BlueHarbor): yes I can share a CICD bucket with prompts, and a spreadsheet with qps by tenant. link will be shared after call.
[07:10] (brief crosstalk)
[07:25] Maya (Redwood): Commercially — we typically run pilot under an evaluation agreement and convert to reserved commit for Dedicated. We can also do a channel rev share for marketplace resell — interested?
[07:38] Priya (BlueHarbor): yes, BlueHarbor marketplace is key to our motion. Let's see the economics; we prefer per-call revenue split over markup.
[07:48] Fatima (BlueHarbor): procurement will need a template contract and an SLA for Dedicated.
[07:56] Maya (Redwood): We'll attach a template during follow-up; also include a sample SLA.
[08:06] Jonas (BlueHarbor): Any gotchas around model licensing for distributing tuned models through your runtime?
[08:15] Kelsey (Redwood): Licensing depends on model license; for customer-owned models we support private deployments. for marketplace-distributed tuned artifacts we need redistribution rights; we'll run a legal check.
[08:28] Ethan (BlueHarbor): What about telemetry and PII — can telemetry be redacted before it leaves BlueHarbor network?
[08:36] Derek (Redwood): Yes, we can redact or obfuscate sensitive fields at the edge. We can show the redaction pattern in the pilot.
[08:48] Priya (BlueHarbor): Ideal timeline — pilot kickoff first week of Sept, run 4 weeks, decision mid-Oct. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:58] Maya (Redwood): We can meet that timeline; Derek will need access to testbed credentials and sample data this week.
[09:06] (Minor background noise)
[09:22] Derek (Redwood): Notes about perf test — we'll provision a 4x H100 NVLink cluster in our staging and run microbenchmarks: latency distributions, cold start, kv cache hit ratios. we'll also test with simulated multi-tenant noise.
[09:36] Jonas (BlueHarbor): For sim multi-tenant, we can provide synthetic traffic patterns and percentiles.
[09:45] Kelsey (Redwood): We'll also test autoscaling and warm pool behavior; important to see billing impact of warm vs cold.
[09:55] Priya (BlueHarbor): On support — we want a single POC contact and an escalation path for 24/7 incidents during pilot.
[10:04] Maya (Redwood): I'll be your primary AE contact; Derek will be SE lead and Kelsey on integration. We'll propose an on-call rotation for critical incidents.
[10:18] Fatima (BlueHarbor): procurement question repeat: what is termination terms for pilot? we need a 14-day opt-out.
[10:27] Maya (Redwood): 14-day opt-out is fine for pilot; we'll put that in the eval agreement.
[10:35] (pause)
[10:50] Priya (BlueHarbor): Anything else from your side?
[10:55] Derek (Redwood): One more technical note — model quantization across NVLink sometimes requires careful chunking of KV cache to avoid cross-GPU jitter. we'll detail best practices.
[11:10] Jonas (BlueHarbor): Good. Also curious about observability hooks — do you expose per-route traces and token-level cost breakdowns?
[11:20] Kelsey (Redwood): Yes, console has token-level cost, per-route latency, and tracing hooks. We'll share screenshots.
[11:33] Maya (Redwood): Okay wrap up — I'll send the SOC2 summary and the partnership deck, Derek will schedule bench run and we aim to kick pilot week of Sept 4th.
[11:44] Priya (BlueHarbor): Great thanks, looking forward.
[11:48] Maya (Redwood): Thanks everyone.
